problem_text:
A logistics company needs to coordinate 7 delivery trucks across 7 different distribution centers.

Each truck must follow a predetermined route represented as pairs (Distribution Center, Handling time),
where each pair specifies the distribution center where the truck must stop and the time required to handle its cargo.
The order of pairs indicates the mandatory sequence of stops each truck must follow.

Truck schedules:
* Truck 1 follows the route: (DC4, 9) → (DC7, 3) → (DC5, 4) → (DC1, 10) → (DC3, 3) → (DC2, 2) → (DC6, 10)
* Truck 2 follows the route: (DC4, 1) → (DC3, 9) → (DC6, 2) → (DC5, 1) → (DC1, 5) → (DC2, 3) → (DC7, 3)
* Truck 3 follows the route: (DC7, 3) → (DC5, 6) → (DC2, 10) → (DC1, 2) → (DC6, 2) → (DC4, 6) → (DC3, 4)
* Truck 4 follows the route: (DC3, 6) → (DC4, 8) → (DC7, 7) → (DC6, 7) → (DC2, 9) → (DC1, 8) → (DC5, 9)
* Truck 5 follows the route: (DC4, 3) → (DC5, 2) → (DC1, 3) → (DC2, 3) → (DC6, 1) → (DC7, 7) → (DC3, 10)
* Truck 6 follows the route: (DC1, 8) → (DC6, 7) → (DC7, 10) → (DC3, 6) → (DC4, 10) → (DC2, 8) → (DC5, 9)
* Truck 7 follows the route: (DC3, 6) → (DC2, 9) → (DC5, 1) → (DC1, 4) → (DC7, 10) → (DC6, 2) → (DC4, 8)

Each truck's cargo handling must proceed continuously once it begins at a distribution center and cannot be interrupted,
and each distribution center can only handle one truck at a time.
The objective is to determine the scheduling sequence for all trucks at the distribution centers
so that the total completion time for all delivery routes is minimized.
